newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends sharply higher.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended sharply higher Friday, with all delivery months out to January 1999, seeing new contract highs, as funds ignored plentiful current sugar supplies and began pricing in a potential supply deficit next season.

"Even though there is no shortage immediately, there is ongoing concern about how the El Nino weather pattern will affect sugar crops in Thailand, Australia and Asia in general, so CSCE sugar continued to go up on fears of shortages down the road," Refco analyst Anne Prendergast said.

"Though there is still a lot of nearby sugar around for delivery and offtake has been poor for most of the summer, but demand is expected to pick up in the fall and the funds have been buying it up anticipating the deficit conditions," she said.
CSCE October sugar ended up 0.31 cent at 11.86 cents a pound, after seeing a new contract high at 11.93 cents, the highest level in nearby CSCE sugar since last October.
The October/March spread narrowed to 0.18 cent, up from a low of 0.28 cent on Monday.

Earlier London trade house C. Czarnikow said world sugar consumption continues to grow and in calendar year 1998 could be 124.4 million tonnes, up from 122.0 million in 1997 and 119.7 million in 1996.

Czarnikow put world sugar production in 1997/98 at 123.3 million tonnes, slightly up from last year's figure of 123.1 million tonnes, but the change masked the huge decline that had occurred in India where the crop has dropped by 6.2 million tonnes raw value.
As a result Carnikow estimates a draw in stocks in the coming cycle of 1.87 million tonnes, compared with a revised increase in stocks for 1996/97 of 0.37 million tonnes.

But in other news, Russian Agriculture Minister Viktor Khystun said the Russian sugar beet harvest should equal or surpass that of last year. Last year Russia produced 16.1 million tonnes of beet sugar.
Continued Russian buying of raw sugar for its mills had earlier been a supportive factor for sugar prices in recent weeks, analysts said.
